n: Edward Partridge, a hatter from Painesville, Ohio, came with Sidney Rigdon to investigate Joseph and was baptized in December 1830. The Lord, “the Mighty One of Israel,” forgives his sins and calls him to preach.

f.g: Edward Partridge, later called as the first bishop of the Church.

n: Through Sidney Rigdon’s hands, Edward will receive the Holy Ghost, who teaches the “peaceable things of the kingdom.”

f.w: the peaceable things of the kingdom

n: Edward is to proclaim loudly: “Hosanna, blessed be the name of the most high God.”

f.g: Hebrew, “save now”; a shout of praise.

n: This call is now extended to all men.
Whoever comes to Joseph and Sidney embracing this call may be ordained and sent to preach among the nations.
Their message: save yourselves from this corrupt generation; come out of the fire, avoiding even what is stained by sin.

f.w: Save yourselves from this untoward generation
hating even the garments spotted with the flesh

n: Every elder who embraces this call with a sincere heart may be ordained and sent out.
Jesus Christ says to prepare, for he will come suddenly to his temple — a prophecy from Malachi.

f.w: I will suddenly come to my temple
